text:
Alex Chen: Quick Q — using the Node SDK streaming sample and my requests get 401 intermittently. I tracked it to our CI-stored API key.
Maria Gomez: Did you confirm there isn't a trailing newline in the secret? windows files often include CRLF.
Alex Chen: I think so. In the CI runner we echo the secret into a file then base64 it for Basic auth: `AUTH=$(cat /tmp/apikey | base64)`
Samir Patel: `cat` will include newline unless created with `echo -n`. On Linux `echo -n` or `printf` avoids newline. On Windows runners `setx` adds a newline to the file sometimes.
Alex Chen: Ah — I tried `echo $API_KEY > /tmp/apikey` — that added `\\n`. Switching to `printf "%s" "$API_KEY" > /tmp/apikey` fixed it for me.
Jules (infra): Also watch out with PowerShell: `Set-Content` appends newlines by default. Use `-NoNewline` or `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText('C:\\apik','...')`.
Maria Gomez: Another quick check: decode your stored header to confirm. `echo $HEADER | base64 --decode` should equal just the key (no `\\n`).
Alex Chen: I did `echo $AUTH | base64 --decode` and got `my-key\\r` — so CR present. `tr -d '\\r'` solved it in our pipeline.
ci-bot: Deploy pipeline: secret rotate job triggered for service `sdk-samples` :white_check_mark:
Samir Patel: For Node SDK docs we should add a snippet about writing secrets without newline and a Windows note. @Maria can you add a line in quickstart?
Maria Gomez: Yep, I'll add a short note and a PowerShell example. Thanks for the reproduce steps, Alex :pray:
